headline: High-risk write and API overlap: Devin can modify shared workspaces and issue-tracking systems while plano can send broad network traffic, creating dangerous interaction paths; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read files, use MCP, and act autonomously in shared integrations; plano can call an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and handle logs/config, so malicious content could flow from Devin into plano or vice versa through shared artifacts. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Devin writes attacker-controlled instructions into shared docs or tickets that plano later ingests as prompts
IF plano forwards untrusted model output into Devin-managed integrations without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of shared docs into prompts
Add a provenance tag to all cross-agent artifacts
Require manual review before either agent consumes the other's output
Restrict MCP endpoints to allowlisted tools
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the integration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs with broad network egress; plano touches logs, traces, and metrics with broad egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive data can move between them and out to external services. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository, ticket queue, or chat thread
IF either agent is configured to forward raw context or logs to its backend
mitigations: Separate credentials and workspaces per agent
Redact secrets from logs before either agent sees them
Turn off sharing of raw traces and metrics
Review outbound destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce tenant isolation at the workspace layer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad shell/network access in a cloud workspace; plano can also make outbound API calls and read config. If both operate on the same repo or mutable resource, Devin can overwrite state while plano concurrently routes or mutates requests, creating an unsafe default conflict. Lack of documented locking pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents are assigned the same git repository or shared config file
IF no external lock or lease is enforced on mutable resources
mitigations: Assign disjoint repos or directories
Pause one agent during writes by the other
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Add a manual lock step before edits
requires-engineering: implement resource leasing for shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can produce code, docs, and tickets; plano is an AI gateway/router that can act on prompts and logs. If plano treats Devin's output as authoritative, errors can cascade from generated content into downstream routing or actions. The profiles do not show explicit verification, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF plano uses Devin-generated text as routing policy or prompt content without validation
IF Devin's generated artifacts are consumed by plano as ground truth
mitigations: Insert a human review gate between agents
Require schema validation on Devin outputs
Compare outputs against source-of-truth data before acting
Limit plano to read-only handling of Devin artifacts
requires-engineering: add automated verification and rollback for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles repo deploy keys, integration tokens, and team chat/docs, while plano is documented only as touching logs, traces, metrics, and config. A compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated data enters plano's telemetry, but the profiles do not show PHI or EU PII, so this is a low-confidence, low-severity residency/retention concern.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in Devin-managed docs, chat, or tickets and is copied into plano logs or traces
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts or logs
Mask identifiers before sending data to plano
Document retention settings for both systems
Review data residency for any telemetry export
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both agents
